Hi Jamie — quick response to your two items, and attaching a concise comparison matrix and sample RCA.

1) Support SLA differences (high-level):
- Redwood: Severity 1 (service down impacting production): initial acknowledgment < 15 mins (pager), incident triage within 1 hour, targeted preliminary RCA within 48 hours, final RCA within 7 business days for infrastructure-related outages. 24/7 on-call rotation + dedicated escalation path for enterprise Dedicated/Private customers.
- Hyperscalers (typical managed endpoints): initial acknowledgment often via ticketing portal 15–60 mins (varies by support tier), triage timelines more variable, preliminary RCA timelines often longer (3–10 business days) and final RCAs frequently limited or high-level for managed control-plane incidents.
- Other inference APIs: mixed — some provide 24/7 response but lack deterministic escalation and on-prem escalation practices we run for Private deployments.

2) Failover behavior: for the pilot we can do an in-region pool failover (automatic within the pool) or cross-region fallback. Given your residency constraints, recommended approach: run the pilot within your region (no cross-region failover) and validate automatic fallback between Dedicated instances / compatible model variants. Cross-region fallover requires contract-level allowances.

Attached: redwood_vs_hyperscalers.xlsx (matrix) and sample_RCA_redacted.txt

If helpful, Priyom can run a short walkthrough on Thursday to explain the RCA format and what evidence we collect.

Thanks,
Rishi
